examples.original: Pon la televisión para ver las noticias.
examples.translated: Put the television on to watch the news.

examples.original: ¿Ponemos la calefacción?
examples.translated: Shall we turn the heating on?

examples.original: Si tengo un niño le pondré Manuel, que es el nombre de mi padre.
examples.translated: If I have a boy, I'll call him Manuel, which is my father's name.

examples.original: ¿Qué nombre le van a poner a la niña? - Todavía no lo sabemos.
examples.translated: What name are you going to give your baby? - We don't know yet.

examples.original: Sandy y su esposo van a poner una panadería en la calle principal.
examples.translated: Sandy and her husband are going to open a bakery on main street.

examples.original: No te pongas impaciente conmigo cuando no has hecho nada para ayudar.
examples.translated: Don't get impatient with me when you haven't done anything to help.

examples.original: No te pongas triste, cariño. Todo se arreglará.
examples.translated: Don't be sad, sweetie. Everything will work out.

examples.original: Me pongo furiosa con pensarlo.
examples.translated: It makes me mad to think about it.

examples.original: El perro siempre se pone feliz al verte.
examples.translated: The dog's always happy to see you.

examples.original: Se pone blando cuando se cocina.
examples.translated: It turns soft when cooked.

examples.original: Ponte la gabardina, está lloviendo.
examples.translated: Put your raincoat on. It's raining.

examples.original: Ya nunca me pongo ese vestido porque se ha quedado muy anticuado.
examples.translated: I don't wear that dress anymore because it's very old-fashioned.

examples.original: Ponte un poco más a la derecha.
examples.translated: Move a little more to the right.

examples.original: El sol se pone y entonces cae la noche.
examples.translated: The sun sets and then night falls.

examples.original: Según se cree, este nuevo actor copará todos los premios este año.
examples.translated: The newcomer is expected to make a clean sweep of all the movie awards this year.

examples.original: El equipo de gimnasia de Estados Unidos copó la mayor cantidad de medallas de oro en los Juegos Olímpicos.
examples.translated: The US gymnastics team took the most gold medals at the Olympic Games.

examples.original: Los juegos coparon las noticias y no hubo mucha información acerca de otros sucesos.
examples.translated: The games monopolized the news and there was little coverage of anything else.

examples.original: No puedes copar la reunión entera con tus propuestas.
examples.translated: You can't monopolise the whole meeting with your proposals.

examples.original: La China está copando los mercados de minerales de tierras raras en África.
examples.translated: China is cornering the rare-earth minerals markets in Africa.

examples.original: Los fans de la cantante coparon completamente la sala de conciertos.
examples.translated: The singer's fans filled the concert hall completely.

examples.original: La patrulla militar copó los puestos enemigos en una maniobra furtiva.
examples.translated: The military patrol took the enemy's posts in a stealth maneuver.

examples.original: Tengo copas de vino suficientes para seis personas.
examples.translated: I have enough wine glasses for six people.

examples.original: ¿Por qué no salimos a tomar unas copas esta noche?
examples.translated: Why don't we go out for some drinks tonight?

examples.original: Para mí, no fue una sorpresa que Alemania ganara la Copa Mundial.
examples.translated: For me, it wasn't a surprise that Germany won the World Cup.

examples.original: El sombrero mexicano es conocido por su copa alta y cónica.
examples.translated: The Mexican sombrero is known for its tall, conical crown.

examples.original: Había un cardenal posado en la copa del árbol.
examples.translated: There was a cardinal perched at the top of the tree.

evidence.source_ingest: direct immutable source, line-extraction, and optional alignment records
evidence.normalization: preserved claims from two immutable legacy evidence runs
evidence.clean_processing: direct immutable tokenization and language-adapter normalization lineage
evidence.routing: direct policy evaluation with a per-word trace and pinned legacy snapshot comparison
evidence.lexical_menu: direct provider-neutral menu candidates; lookup identity remains separate from surface identity
evidence.wsd: complete imported occurrence-level results from one exact method and asset set; no historical assignment fallback

limitations: The legacy ledger recorded language as 'und'; this adapter supplies 'es' from the selected artist release.
The two legacy normalization runs remain the historical comparison; clean processing is a new directly reproducible run.
App assignments are current materialized release records, not invented historical run events.
The clean lexical layer exposes complete provider menus and explicit abstentions; the selected sense is shown only where the imported WSD result binds to that exact menu.
